content.thinking: The savings-fund page shows a +900 ₪ monthly employer contribution and an "מומלץ" tag on a fund called "א. מגדלי מטבעות"; I'm skipping the grey S&P500 text further down.

Each shekel you deposited becomes 3.70 ₪ in the fund and 1.09 ₪ in the securities account. The table shows a −13,974 ₪ tax-on-withdrawal line in the fund column, which worries me, though the bottom line is still higher.
At six years the fund shows 98,738 ₪ against 23,973 ₪ and no striped coins remain, so no tax applies then. I'm checking the "ב. מדרגות" line next, which reads "קרן בלי המעסיק".
The waterfall chart's steps show values like +527, +60,365 and −13,974, and the floating boxes and five-colour legend are confusing me. I'm going to check the chart's legend and axis setup next.
The chart is too busy for me to read, but the three figures at the bottom are clear: 66,513 ₪, 18,000 ₪ and 19,595 ₪. I'm going with the coins for this one.

input.answer: I'd pick the coins, option א. Big piles of coins side by side with one big number under each, 66,513 ₪ against 19,595 ₪, and right away I could see the employer's money makes the fund worth it.

stuck.why: A minus sign, −13,974 ₪, sits in the fund's own column, the side I'm supposed to like. It scared me for a moment until I saw the bottom line was still bigger.
The boxes float in the air at different heights, and there's a red striped box with −13,974. I didn't understand why they don't start from the bottom.
Five colours in the legend plus a white line. Grey, yellow and turquoise all piled on each other is too much for me.
